hero.eyebrow: A research desk for everything you save
hero.sub: Save anything worth reading. The Lede reads it closely, unburies the real story, files it by beat, and writes the strongest honest case the piece can make. Your queue becomes a magazine, not a pile of tabs.

signup.topEyebrow: Out now on the App Store
signup.closingHeading: Start with the next thing you save.
signup.closingSub: Nothing to sign up for and no password to make. Your library lives in your own iCloud, and your first ten briefs each month are free.
signup.disclaimer: Free to start: ten briefs a month, no account. Requires iOS 26. United States App Store.

notes.heading: Occasional notes from the desk
notes.sub: A short note when something meaningful ships. No launch spam; the launch is over.

showcase1.heading: Your saves file themselves into a magazine.
showcase1.body: Every story comes back renamed for what it’s actually about and shelved on its beat. The queue reads like sections you pick by mood.

showcase2.heading: The strongest honest case, before you commit to the read.
showcase2.body: Every save comes back as a short brief: the fairest version of the argument, enough to know what you’re dealing with. When something matters, send The Lede out to dig deeper: more reporting, other angles, an honest bottom line. It works the same on a news story, a how-to, or the history thread you fell into at midnight.
showcase2.featureHeading: It reaches past the source when it has to.
showcase2.featureBody: The Lede holds a standard for the reporting it briefs from. When the strongest account sits with a source it doesn’t trust, it builds the brief from a more solid one, and tells you it did. We explain exactly where that line is on the Sourcing standards page.

founderNote.quote: “I built The Lede because I got tired of headlines that bury the story, or sell one that isn’t there.”
founderNote.attribution: Charles Klein, maker of The Lede
